summary.text: Transpiration is the movement of water through a plant and its evaporation from aerial parts such as leaves, stems and flowers.
It is a passive process that needs no energy from the plant, and it also cools the plant and enables mass flow of mineral nutrients.
Water leaving through small pores called stomata pulls more water up the xylem, because water molecules stick together.

facts.label: Energy cost
facts.value: None, because it is a passive process

facts.label: An acre of corn
facts.value: Gives off about 3,000–4,000 US gallons a day

facts.label: Large oak tree
facts.value: Can transpire 40,000 US gallons per year

facts.label: Transpiration ratio
facts.value: Crops lose 200 to 1000 kg of water per kg of dry matter

items.prompt: On a hot day a plant's roots take up less water than its leaves lose. What does the plant do to cut the loss?

options.label: It opens its pores wider to cool itself
It closes its stomata, which also slows nutrient uptake
It pumps water upward using extra energy
It stops all water moving in the xylem

items.explain: When uptake falls behind loss, plants close their stomata to decrease water loss, which also slows nutrient uptake and carbon dioxide absorption.

items.prompt: As water evaporates from a leaf, it tugs on the water behind it all the way down the stem. What property of water makes this possible?

options.label: Its molecules stick together
The plant pumps it using the roots' energy
Its weight pulls it toward the leaf
Evaporation makes the water denser

items.explain: Water molecules stick together, so one evaporating from the leaf surface pulls on its neighbour, creating a continuous flow through the plant.

items.prompt: Some desert plants keep their pores shut by day and open them at night. What does this gain them?

options.label: Roots absorb water faster in the dark
Photosynthesis needs no carbon dioxide at night
Closed pores make daytime growth quicker
Less water is lost, since transpiration is lower at night

items.explain: In CAM photosynthesis, the stomata are closed during the day and open at night, when transpiration will be lower.

items.prompt: How does a plant speed up or slow down the water it loses through its leaves?

options.label: By making its xylem water heavier
By switching its roots on and off
By changing how sticky its water is
By changing how wide its stomatal openings are

items.explain: Plants regulate the rate of transpiration by controlling the size of the stomatal apertures.

items.prompt: A plant cannot take in enough water to keep up with its losses. What goes wrong inside its xylem?

options.label: Water vapor fills it and forms blockages
It fills with extra water and bursts
Its stomata seal shut for good
Its cohesion makes the water flow faster

items.explain: When a plant cannot supply enough water, cavitation occurs: the xylem fills with water vapor that forms blockages and stops water transport.

items.prompt: What lets a very tall tree lift water against gravity up to its highest leaves?

options.label: Pressure that builds up in the roots and pushes sap upward
A pump in the trunk powered by the plant
The drop in pressure at the top as water diffuses out of the stomata
Capillary action alone, with no pressure difference

items.explain: In tall plants and trees, gravity can be overcome only by the decrease in hydrostatic pressure in the upper parts as water diffuses out of the stomata.
